text:
andrew: Quick sync — we need to pick a primary internal API shape for console -> runtime/control-plane traffic. Rest vs gRPC, protobufs, gateway translation, and how routing/quotas/telemetry plug in. High-level preferences?

sophie: lean gRPC for runtime RPCs. streaming + bidi useful for logs/streaming tokens, and typed contracts avoid subtle regressions. also easier to enforce method-level SLOs. :+1:

raj: agree on typed contracts, but browser/console clients still expect JSON/REST. we can't force gRPC in the frontend without a proxy or grpc-web shim. that's a big UX lift. :thinking:

lisa: pragmatic approach: gRPC for backend-to-backend, REST/grpc-web for frontend. put a thin gateway at the edge that handles transcode and auth. gateway should be stateless and just translate + inject routing headers.

andrew: how do we carry routing policy info (route weights, tier, fallback hints) across the boundary? headers? body envelope?

sophie: headers is cleaner. keep the request payload pure. e.g.:

```
X-Redwood-Tenant: tenant_123
X-Redwood-Route: llm-prod-v1
X-Redwood-Route-Weight: 80
X-Redwood-Trace-Id: 01abc...
```

lisa: +1 for headers. gateway can map higher-level route names to actual model variants. it also helps quota middleware to apply tenant-specific limits before traffic hits the runtime.

raj: quotas are tricky — enforcement at the gateway is easiest for surface-level rate limits, but token-level accounting (per model/token) needs to be emitted from the runtime. we should standardize a telemetry envelope for billing events.

sophie: propose two-layer quota model: 1) permissive/gateway-level quick-fail for obvious rate limits, 2) authoritative accounting events from runtime (via kafka/metrics) that feed billing/console. both layers emit the same request_id so we can reconcile.

andrew: rollout UX question: when we switch an endpoint from REST->gRPC (or add gRPC only method), how do we avoid breaking third parties and console?

lisa: gradual: support both routes on the gateway for a few weeks, use header X-Redwood-API-Version and prefer new route only for canary tenants. console gets an opt-in toggle in the UI. we also surface telemetry dashboard for errors and latencies per transport.

raj: on telemetry: we need per-transport latency histograms, transcode overhead, and sampling of payloads for regressions. make it easy to query "latency by transport and route" in the console.

sophie: also include small synthetic traces for canary flows every minute. flag any  p50/p95 regressions > 20% automatically.

andrew: does anyone object to protobufs as the canonical schema and codegen for server/server calls?

lisa: protobufs yes, but we should keep a lightweight JSON schema for frontend validation and docs. auto-generate JSON OpenAPI snippets from proto for the console docs.

raj: client SDK story: generate both typed gRPC clients and fetch-friendly JS wrappers that use grpc-web/fallback to REST. ship the wrappers to console team so they don't have to maintain two code paths.

sophie: ops considerations: include 3 headers for telemetry: X-Redwood-Trace-Id, X-Redwood-Route, X-Redwood-Client-Version. ensure gateway copies them into runtime metadata so we don't lose observability.

lisa: also add a lightweight quota-feedback header from runtime -> gateway when a request is throttled: X-Redwood-Quota-Remaining and X-Redwood-Quota-Reset. that makes UX for the console nicer (we can show live quota meters).

andrew: security question: are we comfortable with route names being visible in headers? any leakage concerns?

sophie: route names are internal identifiers; gateway enforces tenancy scoping. if we worry, we can hash route names for outbound telemetry but keep mapping internally.

raj: example cURL for fallback mode (for engineers):

```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
     -H "X-Redwood-Route: llm-prod-v1" \
     -H "X-Redwood-Trace-Id: $(uuidgen)" \
     https://edge.redwood.internal/v1/generate
```

andrew: action items:
- lisa: prototype gateway transcode mapping + header passthrough (this week)
- sophie: spec for telemetry/envelope + synthetic canary checks (this week)
- raj: client wrapper proposal for console SDKs (next week)
- andrew: doc with migration plan + rollout steps for API versioning (next week)

deploy-bot: Scheduled canary job created: canary/api-transport-checks -> starts in 2h (ID: cj-8801). :white_check_mark:

lisa: cool — i'll push a minimal PR to the gateway repo with proto -> rest mapping and a README showing header invariants. won't flip anything without the rollout doc.

andrew: perfect. we'll reconvene after the prototypes. thanks all. :rocket:
